newsitem.title: ITALY: Fiat slips after good run, CSFB downgrade.
newsitem.headline: Fiat slips after good run, CSFB downgrade.

text.p: Shares in Italian industrial and automotive group Fiat slipped on Monday after a strong run up over the last few weeks and an earnings downgrade from investment bank CS First Boston, dealers said.
There was also some caution ahead of expected first nine month 1996 figures expected later on Monday after a board meeting, and which are set to be published after the bourse closes.
At 1530 GMT, Fiat shares were off 3.2 percent at 4,385 lire in a largely steady Milan bourse with trading volume just under six million shares.
Dealers said the shares had risen over the last few weeks from an all-time low of 3,920 lire, and some operators were thinking the rise had gone far enough for now.
CS First Boston said it had downgraded its earnings forecasts for Fiat in 1996 and 1997 due to a continuing depressed Italian domestic car market and the high value of the lira.
